43% [[humidity]]{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/newsfiles/UCL/2026/2047742_LU.pdf |title=Tactical Line-ups – Final – Saturday 30 May 2026 |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=30 May 2026 |access-date=30 May 2026}} | previous = [[2025 UEFA Champions League final|2025]] | next = ''[[2027 UEFA Champions League final|2027]]'' }} The '''2026 UEFA Champions League final''' was the final match of the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League]], the 71st season of Europe's premier club [[association football|football]] tournament organised by [[UEFA]], and the 34th season since it was renamed from the [[European Champion Clubs' Cup]] to the [[UEFA Champions League]]. It was played at the [[Puskás Aréna]] in [[Budapest]], Hungary, on 30 May 2026 between French club [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]], the defending champions, and English club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]. This was the first final to include a titleholder team since [[2018 UEFA Champions League final|2018]]. This was Arsenal’s first [[List of European Cup and UEFA Champions League finals|Champions League Final]] appearance since [[2006 UEFA Champions League final|2006]], where they lost to [[FC Barcelona]] 2-1. Paris Saint-Germain won the match 4–3 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]], following a 1–1 draw after [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]], for their second UEFA Champions League title, becoming the second club to win back-to-back titles in the UEFA Champions League era, matching [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]'s feat in the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League|2016–17 edition]].{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/02a5-20c02e59f219-15e92acdc717-1000/ |title=Paris retain Champions League: Holders edge Arsenal on penalties |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=30 May 2026 |access-date=30 May 2026}}{{cite web |title=Champions League holders: Paris join Real Madrid as back-to-back winners |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0239-0e96d80bc2f6-d4e7f311245e-1000/ |date=30 May 2026 |access-date=31 May 2026 |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations}} As winners, Paris Saint-Germain earned the right to play against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], the winners of the [[2025–26 UEFA Europa League]], in the [[2026 UEFA Super Cup]]. They will also compete in the final of the [[2026 FIFA Intercontinental Cup]], and qualified for the [[2029 FIFA Club World Cup]]. ==Background== [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] reached their third European Cup/Champions League final overall and second consecutively, having lost to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in [[2020 UEFA Champions League final|2020]] before winning the title in [[2025 UEFA Champions League final|2025]]. They also became the first team since [[Liverpool FC|Liverpool]] in [[2018 UEFA Champions League final|2018]] and [[2019 UEFA Champions League final|2019]] to reach two consecutive Champions League finals. This was their seventh UEFA competition final overall, having also triumphed in the [[1996 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup final]] and [[2025 UEFA Super Cup]]. They lost the Cup Winners' Cup final in [[1997 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup final|1997]] as holders, as well as losing the [[1996 UEFA Super Cup]]. Paris Saint-Germain was the first French team to appear in three European Cup/Champions League finals, surpassing their [[Le Classique|rivals]] [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], who lost in [[1991 European Cup final|1991]] before their victory in [[1993 UEFA Champions League final|1993]], as well as [[Stade de Reims|Stade Reims]], who lost both the [[1956 European Cup final|1956]] and [[1959 European Cup final|1959]] European Cup finals to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]. [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] reached their second European Cup/Champions League final, having lost to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in [[2006 UEFA Champions League final|2006]]. This was their eighth UEFA competition final overall, having triumphed in the [[1994 European Cup Winners' Cup final]]. They lost the Cup Winners' Cup finals in [[1980 European Cup Winners' Cup final|1980]] and [[1995 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup final|1995]]—the latter as holders, as well as losing the [[1994 European Super Cup]], [[2000 UEFA Cup final]], and [[2019 UEFA Europa League final]]. Both clubs won their respective leagues and were eliminated from other cup competitions, thus aiming for a [[Double (association football)#Continental double|continental double]]. This was the first time since [[2020 UEFA Champions League final|2020]] where both Champions League finalists were champions of their respective domestic leagues. The two teams met in the 2025 semi-finals, with Paris Saint-Germain winning both legs (1–0 at the [[Emirates Stadium]] and then 2–1 at the [[Parc des Princes]]). The 2026 final was the fourth European Cup final between sides from two different capital cities after [[1962 European Cup final|1962]], [[1966 European Cup final|1966]] and [[1971 European Cup final|1971]].{{cite web |last=Anand |first=Anish |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48699334/uefa-champions-league-stats-kvaratskhelia-record-seven-game-streak-dembele-16-goal-contributions-arsenal-unbeaten-14 |title=UCL stats: Kvaratskhelia's record seven-game streak, Dembélé's 16 goal contributions, Arsenal unbeaten in 14 |work=ESPN |date=7 May 2026 }} The "home" team (for administrative purposes) was predetermined as the winners of semi-final 1 (Paris Saint-Germain). This was the first Champions League final to kick off at 18:00 [[Central European Summer Time|CEST]], three hours earlier than previous editions. UEFA stated that the change was made to "enhance the matchday experience and benefit fans, teams and host cities".{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/029c-1e9620d873ad-b9d62ed347c6-1000/ |title=UEFA Champions League final kick-off moves to 18:00CET as of 2025/26 season |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=28 August 2025 |access-date=17 September 2025}}{{Cite web |last1=Zelealem |first1=Fasika |last2=Davies |first2=Mathew |date=6 May 2026 |title=When is the Champions League final? Location and ticket information |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/champions-league-final-location-ticket-33896709 |access-date=30 May 2026 |website=Wales Online |language=en}} ===Previous finals=== ''In the following table, finals until 1992 were in the European Cup era and since 1993 were in the UEFA Champions League era.'' {| class="wikitable" |- !Team !Previous final appearances (bold indicates winners) |- |{{#invoke:flag|fbaicon|FRA}} [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] |2 ([[2020 UEFA Champions League final|2020]], '''[[2025 UEFA Champions League final|2025]]''') |- |{{#invoke:flag|fbaicon|ENG}} [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] |1 ([[2006 UEFA Champions League final|2006]]) |} ==Venue== [[File:Puskás Aréna 03.jpg|thumb|upright=1.2|The [[Puskás Aréna]] in [[Budapest]] hosted the final.]] ===Host selection=== On 17 May 2023, UEFA opened the bidding process for the final, which was held in parallel with that of the [[2027 UEFA Champions League final|2027 final]]. Interested bidders could bid for either one or both of the finals. Additionally, bidding associations could only be appointed one UEFA final in a given year. The proposed venues had to include natural grass and be ranked as a [[UEFA stadium categories|UEFA category four stadium]], with a gross capacity of at least 70,000 preferred. [[Vitinha (footballer, born February 2000)|Vitinha]] (left) was named [[Player of the match#Association football|man of the match]], while his opponent midfielder [[Kai Havertz]] (right) scored the earliest goal of the match. }} In the sixth minute of the match, an attempted [[glossary_of_association_football_terms#C|clearance]] by Paris Saint-Germain defender [[Marquinhos]] deflected off Arsenal's [[Leandro Trossard]]. The deflected ball fell to Arsenal striker [[Kai Havertz]], who beat the Paris Saint-Germain goalkeeper [[Matvey Safonov]] from a tight angle, putting Arsenal 1–0 ahead. It would be their only shot on target throughout the match.{{Cite web |title=PSG beat Arsenal on penalties to defend Champions League title |url=https://www.espn.com/football/report/_/gameId/401862897 |date=30 May 2026 |access-date=5 June 2026 |website=ESPN }} In the 61st minute, Arsenal's [[Cristhian Mosquera]] fouled [[Khvicha Kvaratskhelia]] inside the [[penalty box]]. [[Ousmane Dembélé]] converted the resulting penalty kick, tying the score at 1–1. In the 77th minute, a shot by Kvaratskhelia was deflected onto the post by [[Myles Lewis-Skelly]].{{cite news |last1=Rouse |first1=Daniel |title=Champions League final analysis: PSG beat Arsenal on penalties |url=https://www.thescore.com/chlg/news/3547570/champions-league-final-analysis-psg-beat-arsenal-on-penalties |access-date=10 June 2026 |work=TheScore |date=30 May 2026}} By the end of the second half, Paris Saint-Germain had made 18 attempts on goal (four on target), while Arsenal had made four attempts (one on target). With the score still tied, the game went to [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]]. In the 103rd minute, Paris Saint-Germain's [[Nuno Mendes (footballer, born 2002)|Nuno Mendes]] tackled [[Noni Madueke]] to the ground in his team's penalty area, prompting appeals for a penalty kick by Arsenal players. However, the referee awarded a [[free kick]] to Paris Saint-Germain instead, adjudging that Madueke had grabbed Mendes' arm,{{cite news |last1=Davies |first1=Andy |title=VAR review: UCL ref got the Mendes-Madueke call right, but it was close |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48923039/var-review-ucl-ref-got-mendes-madueke-call-right-was-close |access-date=10 June 2026 |date=30 May 2026|website=ESPN}} and issued [[Penalty_card#Association_football|yellow card]]s to Arsenal player [[Declan Rice]] and manager [[Mikel Arteta]] for their protests.{{cite news |last1=Hewitt |first1=Matthew |title=Declan Rice and Mikel Arteta explode as Arsenal denied Champions League final penalty |url=https://www.football.london/arsenal-fc/news/arsenal-champions-league-final-psg-34038721 |access-date=10 June 2026 |work=football.London |date=30 May 2026}} Extra time ended with the score tied 1–1 and the match proceeded to a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]]. Paris Saint-Germain went first in the shoot-out, with [[Gonçalo Ramos]] converting his penalty. This was followed by successful attempts by Arsenal's [[Viktor Gyökeres]] and Paris Saint-Germain's [[Désiré Doué]]. The first miss was by Arsenal's [[Eberechi Eze]], who shot wide left, which was immediately followed by Arsenal goalkeeper [[David Raya]] saving Mendes' attempt. Four successful attempts followed, two for each team, by Rice, [[Achraf Hakimi]], [[Gabriel Martinelli]], and [[Lucas Beraldo]], leaving Paris Saint-Germain ahead 4–3 with one penalty attempt to come before the [[Sudden death (sport)|sudden-death round]]. [[Gabriel Magalhães|Gabriel]] sent his shot over the bar, giving Paris Saint-Germain the victory.{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401862897 ==Aftermath== {{Main|2026 Paris Saint-Germain celebration riots}} Following PSG's victory, tens of thousands of fans celebrated on the streets of Paris. Violent clashes erupted as the celebrations developed into rioting; there were 283 arrests in Paris and another 133 in the rest of France.{{Cite web |date=May 31, 2026 |title=Hundreds arrested in Paris after Champions League final |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cg7pk5j7nyjo |access-date=2026-04-06 |website=BBC |language=en-GB|last=Sekulich|first=Harry}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/05/30/dozens-arrested-in-paris-clashes-on-psg-victory-night_6753979_7.html|title=Dozens arrested in Paris clashes on PSG victory night |website=[[Le Monde]] |date=May 30, 2026|access-date=4 June 2026}} The [[Minister of the Interior (France)|French Interior Ministry]] deployed 22,000 security officers across the country, including 8,000 in the capital.
